---
title: "Running with elucidatornf"
---

[elucidatornf](https://github.com/nickjhathaway/elucidatornf) is a set of Nextflow workflows that
run SeekDeep from raw reads to final haplotypes. It is the recommended way to run SeekDeep. It
works out the extraction settings from your primers and reference genomes, runs the samples in
parallel, picks up where it left off with `-resume`, and writes the results as tables, a PMO and
HTML reports.

This page covers what you need to start a run. The
[elucidatornf README](https://github.com/nickjhathaway/elucidatornf#readme) lists every option.

## Setup

You need [Nextflow](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/install.html) 24.04.2 or newer and either
Docker or Apptainer/Singularity. The workflows pull the container with SeekDeep in it, so you don't
need to [install SeekDeep](../install.qmd) yourself.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/nickjhathaway/elucidatornf.git
```

## What you give it

| Input | Flag | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Reads | `--input_fastq_dir` | Illumina: paired `*_R1*.fastq.gz`/`*_R2*.fastq.gz`, one pair per sample. Nanopore: fastq files and/or unaligned bams from `dorado demux`. |
| Primers | `--primers_fnp` | Tab-delimited with a header line, three columns: target name, forward primer, reverse primer, both written 5'→3' as ordered. |
| Reference genomes | `--genome_dir` and `--gff_dir`, or `--download_plasmodium_genomes` | Used to find each target's reference sequences and expected lengths. For *Plasmodium*, `--download_plasmodium_genomes` fetches and indexes [plasmodium_genomes](https://github.com/nickjhathaway/plasmodium_genomes) for you. |
| Read length (Illumina) | `--illumina_clustering_paired_end_length` | The length of each mate, e.g. `150` or `250`. Used to work out which targets the mates overlap enough to stitch. |
| Output directory | `--outdir` | |
| Container | `-profile docker` or `-profile apptainer` | |

An example primers file:

```tsv
target	forward	reverse
PFAMA1	CCATCAGGGAAATGTCCAGT	TTTCCTGCATGTCTTGAACA
PFMSP1	AACTAGAAGCTTTAGAAGATGCA	ACATATGATTGGTTAAATCAAAG
```

### Samples, replicates and barcodes

Each fastq pair (Illumina) or demultiplexed barcode (nanopore) becomes one sample, named after the
file. A **sample key** (`--amplicon_sample_key_fnp`) changes that:

- it renames inputs;
- it marks inputs as PCR replicates of one sample, which are clustered separately and combined at
  the population step (by default a haplotype has to be found in every replicate);
- it splits inputs that pool several samples with in-line barcodes (MIDs).

```tsv
input	sample	replicate	fbarcode	rbarcode
Run1_LibA	P001		ACGTACGTAC	TTGACCATGC
Run1_LibA	P002		TGCATGCATG	CCAGTTGACA
Run2_LibA	P001		ACGTACGTAC	TTGACCATGC
Sample9	P009
```

`SeekDeep getPossibleSampleNamesFromRawInput` lists the input names a directory will give, and
can write a starting sample key:

```bash
SeekDeep getPossibleSampleNamesFromRawInput --inputDir fastq/ --sampleKeyOut sampleKey.tsv
```

The [sample key guide](https://github.com/nickjhathaway/elucidatornf/blob/dev/docs/sample_key.md)
covers the format, how replicates are named and combined, and the checks a key has to pass.

Two related options: `--amplicon_samples_keep_file` processes only the samples listed in it.
`--meta_fnp` attaches a metadata table (a `sample` column plus any others) to the results.

## Illumina

```bash
nextflow run elucidatornf/illumina_clustering.nf \
  --input_fastq_dir fastq/ \
  --primers_fnp primers.tsv \
  --download_plasmodium_genomes \
  --plasmodium_genomes_dir /data/plasmodium_genomes \
  --illumina_clustering_paired_end_length 150 \
  --outdir results \
  -profile docker
```

For non-*Plasmodium* targets, give `--genome_dir` and `--gff_dir` instead of
`--download_plasmodium_genomes`.

Targets too long for their mates to overlap are clustered as `<target>-R1` and `<target>-R2`.
Single-end reads, such as SRA runs whose pairs were merged before upload, take
`--illumina_single_end`.

### Options worth knowing

- `--illumina_clustering_min_sample_read_count` (default 50): replicates with fewer reads for a
  target are left out of population clustering.
- `--illumina_clustering_filter_extracted_reads`: drops extracted reads that don't share enough
  k-mers with their target's reference sequences, such as host reads or primer dimers that carry
  the right primers.
- `--illumina_clustering_read_qc`: also runs [read QC](#read-qc).
- `--do_variant_calling` with `--vc_primary_genome Pf3D7`: calls variants and amino acid changes
  against a reference genome.
- `--amplicon_clustering_pop_clustering_extra_args "..."`: passes extra flags to
  [`processClusters`](../reference/seekdeep.qmd#processClusters).

## Nanopore

```bash
nextflow run elucidatornf/nanopore_clustering.nf \
  --input_fastq_dir demux/ \
  --primers_fnp primers.tsv \
  --download_plasmodium_genomes \
  --plasmodium_genomes_dir /data/plasmodium_genomes \
  --outdir results \
  -profile docker
```

`--input_fastq_dir` is searched recursively. Bams are named by the `SM` of their read group (e.g.
`barcode01`), and `unclassified` files are skipped. To combine several demux runs, point
`--input_fastq_dir` at a directory holding each run's output and add
`--nanopore_sample_name_prefix_top_dir`, which prefixes each sample name with its run directory.

For amplicons that reads often don't cover end to end (rapid barcoding, long targets), reads can
be trimmed to regions inside each target. Give the regions' primers with
`--nanopore_trim_primers_fnp`, or use `--nanopore_extractor_use_inner_primers` to make them from
the ends of each target. The amplified primers are then used only to tell which target a read
comes from, to split reads of several amplicons joined together and to drop foldbacks.

## Read QC {#read-qc}

`illumina_read_qc.nf`, or `--illumina_clustering_read_qc` on a clustering run, runs
[`SeekDeep ampliconReadQC`](../reference/seekdeeputils.qmd#ampliconReadQC). It puts every read
pair into one category (`onTarget`, `primerDimer`, `shortProduct`, `kmerMismatch`,
`mismatchedPrimers` and others) and uses BLAST to work out where unexpected products came from:
another target in the panel, elsewhere in the target genome, the host, or adapter. It only
reports and doesn't change which reads are kept. Results go to `readQC/`.

Every Illumina clustering run also writes a primer dimer report,
`extractionReports/allPrimerDimerCounts.tsv.gz`, with the primers each dimer is made of and their
predicted dimerization scores.

## What you get

| Directory | What's in it |
|---|---|
| `finalResults/` | `allSelectedClustersInfo.tsv.gz` (final haplotypes per sample and target, with frequencies and read counts), `allele_data.tsv.gz`, `allSampleClustersInfo.tsv.gz` and `allPMO.json.gz` (everything as one [PMO](https://plasmogenepi.github.io/PMO_Docs/)) |
| `extractionReports/` | Reads per sample and target at each extraction step, why reads failed, primer dimers, and `outSeekDeepExtractorFlags.txt` (the extractor flags the workflow chose) |
| `primerInfo/` | The primers used and each target's reference sequences and locations in each genome |
| `variantCalls/` | Variant and amino acid change reports, with `--do_variant_calling` |
| `readQC/` | Read QC reports, with `--illumina_clustering_read_qc` |
| `meta/` | `sample_name_key.tsv`: input, sample, replicate and barcodes for every sample with extracted reads |
| `run/`, `pipeline_info/` | The parameters used, run times and Nextflow's execution reports |

To browse the results, see [Viewing results](viewers.qmd).

## Re-running and resources

- Add `-resume` to pick up a run where it stopped. Steps whose inputs haven't changed are reused.
- `--max_task_cpus`, `--max_task_memory` and `--max_executor_cpus` cap the resources used. They
  are clamped to the machine by default.
- On Nextflow 26.04 or newer, turn a boolean flag on by giving it bare (`--do_variant_calling`) and
  off by leaving it out. `--do_variant_calling false` still turns it on, because the CLI value is
  the string `"false"`.
